question: Why do nurses love using infrared thermometers on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: It prints out a paper record automatically
options.B: It captures temperature quickly without touching the skin
options.C: It measures core temperature directly from the heart
options.D: It never needs new batteries or calibration

explanation: You'll find these handy on the ward because they let you screen patients fast without needing physical skin contact. Great for keeping things moving! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h1)

question: Why are infrared thermometers a lifesaver when taking a child's temperature?

options.A: Under-fives cannot register a fever on other devices
options.B: Infrared devices block all room drafts completely
options.C: Children are less likely to get scared or fight you
options.D: Kids' skin always radiates extra heat

explanation: Quick, touch-free readings mean less anxiety and crying for the little ones, making your assessment much smoother! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h1)

question: What type of energy do infrared thermometers pick up from the human body?
explanation: These thermometers are built to sense the invisible heat energy that naturally radiates from warm human skin. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h2)

question: What is the job of the thermopile inside an infrared thermometer?

options.A: It blocks bright room light from entering
options.B: It warms up the lens to match body heat
options.C: It pumps cool air over the computer chips
options.D: It converts absorbed heat into an electrical signal

explanation: Think of the thermopile as a translator: it takes the focused heat energy and turns it into an electrical voltage that the thermometer's screen can read. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h2)

question: Which part of the ear does a tympanic thermometer aim for?
explanation: Tympanic thermometers go gently into the ear canal to pick up heat coming straight off the eardrum. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h3)

question: Why is the eardrum (tympanic membrane) such a great spot to check core body temperature?

options.A: It shares a blood supply with the brain's temperature center
options.B: It is completely protected from any room air
options.D: It always shows the highest temperature on the body

explanation: The eardrum shares blood vessels with the hypothalamus (your body's thermostat), giving you a very true picture of core temperature. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h3)

question: Which of these would stop you from using a tympanic thermometer safely?

options.A: A buildup of earwax blocking the ear canal
options.B: The patient just drank some water
options.C: A history of mild seasonal allergies

explanation: Excess wax blocks the path to the eardrum, meaning the sensor won't catch the right heat radiation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h4)

question: A patient arrives sweating heavily with thick makeup on their forehead. What should you do for their temperature?

options.A: Use the temporal thermometer right over the makeup
options.B: Use another route, like the ear or mouth
options.C: Wipe the forehead with alcohol and read immediately
options.D: Add two degrees to whatever the temporal reading says

explanation: Sweat and cosmetics mess up forehead heat readings. Save yourself a headache and switch to an oral or tympanic route! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h4)

question: How should you position an adult patient's ear before using a tympanic thermometer?

options.C: Press it flat against the side of the head

explanation: Pulling the adult pinna up and back straightens out the curved ear canal so the thermometer has a straight shot at the eardrum. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h5)

question: Why should you wait fifteen minutes to take a patient's temperature if they just rushed in from the hot sun?

options.A: To give the patient time to calm down during triage
options.B: To make sure the disposable probe cover doesn't melt
options.C: To let the thermometer warm up its internal sensors
options.D: To let their skin temperature adjust to the indoor air

explanation: Hot or cold weather temporarily changes surface skin temperature. Giving them a few minutes inside ensures your reading is accurate. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h5)

question: What happens to an infant's temperature reading if they are crying or throwing a tantrum?

options.A: It goes up because of increased facial muscle activity and blood flow
options.B: It causes the device to show an error code
options.C: It drops to a false low because of heavy breathing
options.D: It has no effect at all on infrared readings

explanation: Crying pumps up local blood circulation and muscle work around the face, which can push skin temperatures up temporarily. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h6)

question: Which of these does NOT cause an error when using an infrared thermometer?

options.A: Bringing the device straight from a cold room into a warm ward
options.B: Using a brand new disposable probe cover
options.C: Heavy sweat on the patient's forehead
options.D: Accumulated earwax in the ear canal

explanation: A clean probe cover is what you *want* to use! It keeps things hygienic and won't mess up your reading. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h6)

question: What is the proper way to clean the delicate lens on an infrared thermometer?

options.A: Submerge the whole device in boiling water for five minutes
options.B: Spray high-pressure air directly onto the glass
options.C: Scrub the lens firmly with a scouring pad
options.D: Wipe gently with an approved alcohol wipe following maker instructions

explanation: A gentle wipe with isopropyl alcohol cleans the lens safely without scratching the glass or frying the electronics. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h7)

question: Why is it a big mistake to submerge an infrared thermometer in cleaning liquid?

options.A: It causes the batteries to explode right away
options.B: It ruins the internal electronics and ruins future readings
options.C: It dissolves the outer plastic casing instantly
options.D: It turns the digital display screen permanently black

explanation: Liquid leaking inside will short-circuit the board and mess up the sensitive sensors. Always wipe, never soak! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h7)

question: Why must you always write down the body site (like oral or tympanic) along with the temperature number?

options.A: Different sites use completely different scales like Kelvin
options.B: Electronic health records will lock your chart without it
options.C: Hospital insurance demands the name of the device maker
options.D: Normal body temperature ranges change depending on where you measure it

explanation: Different parts of the body naturally run at slightly different baselines, so knowing the route is vital to read the results correctly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h8)

question: A patient's forehead temperature reads 37.8°C, but they look pale and are shivering hard. What should you suspect?

options.A: The patient has a severe brain injury
options.B: Shivering can make skin feel cold while a real fever is hiding underneath
options.C: The thermometer is definitely broken and should be thrown away
options.D: The patient has no fever at all and needs no more checks

explanation: When shivering causes surface blood vessels to tighten up, skin readings can look normal or low even when core temperature is climbing. Always keep a close eye! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h8)
